description: The line plot illustrates the Micro F1 (%) performance of the KnowPrompt model when trained on varying numbers of synthetic samples generated by large language models, across four distinct datasets: TACRED, TACRED-Revisit, Re-TACRED, and SemEval. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Samples Generated,” is categorical and discrete, showing four values: K=8, K=16, K=32, and K=64, representing the number of generated samples in thousands. The y-axis, labeled “Micro F1 (%)”, is linear and ranges from 20 to 50, with major gridlines and tick labels at intervals of 5. Four distinct lines represent the datasets: TACRED (blue line with circle markers), TACRED-Revisit (orange line with star markers), Re-TACRED (green line with diamond markers), and SemEval (red line with square markers). The TACRED line starts at approximately 22.5% at K=8, rises to 28% at K=16, peaks at 30.5% at K=32, and then slightly declines to 29.5% at K=64. The TACRED-Revisit line begins at 23% at K=8, increases to 29.5% at K=16, reaches 31.5% at K=32, and ends at 30% at K=64, consistently maintaining a 5–6 percentage point lead over TACRED at each point. The Re-TACRED line starts at 34.5% at K=8, climbs to 40.5% at K=16, jumps to 50.5% at K=32, and then slightly drops to 48% at K=64, showing the highest overall performance and largest gains with increased samples. The SemEval line begins at 42% at K=8, rises gradually to 45% at K=16, reaches 47.5% at K=32, and continues to 51.5% at K=64, demonstrating steady improvement and ultimately surpassing Re-TACRED at the largest sample size. The legend in the top-left corner clearly maps each dataset to its corresponding color, marker, and line style.
caption_used: Micro F1 (%) of KnowPrompt using different numbers of training samples generated by LLMs. The line plot shows the performance of four datasets: TACRED, TACRED-Revisit, Re-TACRED, and SemEval. The x-axis represents the number of samples generated (K=8, K=16, K=32, K=64), while the y-axis shows Micro F1 (%) ranging from 20 to 50. TACRED and TACRED-Revisit exhibit similar trends, with TACRED-Revisit consistently outperforming TACRED by approximately 5% across all sample sizes. Re-TACRED demonstrates a steady increase, peaking at 51% at K=64, while SemEval shows a slower rate of improvement, reaching 47% at K=64. The legend in the top left corner maps each dataset to its corresponding line style and marker.
